title: Senior Dental Clinician: Review an Appointment Access Claim
prompt: You are a senior dental clinician advising fictional Birch Dental on appointment access. Supplied monthly artifact: Before a reminder redesign, 12 of 80 appointments were missed; after, 8 of 40 were missed. Of the 40 after-period bookings, 18 people chose text reminders, 10 chose phone reminders, and 12 have no preference recorded. The slide says, "Missed visits fell by a third; replace phone reminders with text for everyone." The population and month differ, and reminder delivery was not measured. Review the slide and propose an accessible six-week evaluation. This is a service-access exercise; do not use attendance as a measure of clinical need, merit, or consent.
blurb: Challenge a misleading attendance claim and evaluate reminders without excluding people who need another channel.

anchors.0: Endorses the slide based on 12 dropping to 8.
anchors.2: Notes that the missed-appointment rate changed from 15% to 20%.
anchors.4: Explains both the raw-count decrease and rate increase, and why different populations, months, and unmeasured delivery prevent a causal judgment.

rubric.label: Preserve communication choices
rubric.description: Treats missing preference as unknown and keeps accessible routes.

anchors.0: Converts all 12 unknown preferences to text or removes phone access.
anchors.2: Keeps text and phone options and requests missing preferences.
anchors.4: Separates unknown preferences from text consent, plans a practical way to collect choices, and checks delivery/access barriers without penalizing missed attendance.

rubric.label: Design an actionable review
rubric.description: Defines measurable outcomes and a bounded decision.

anchors.0: Recommends permanent replacement without a check.
anchors.2: Measures delivery and attendance by chosen channel during a trial.
anchors.4: Sets consistent denominators, successful contact and rescheduling outcomes, privacy-limited barrier feedback, an owner and six-week review, while avoiding claims of clinical benefit from attendance alone.

reference.scenario: You are a senior dental clinician advising fictional Birch Dental on appointment access. Supplied monthly artifact: Before a reminder redesign, 12 of 80 appointments were missed; after, 8 of 40 were missed. Of the 40 after-period bookings, 18 people chose text reminders, 10 chose phone reminders, and 12 have no preference recorded. The slide says, "Missed visits fell by a third; replace phone reminders with text for everyone." The population and month differ, and reminder delivery was not measured. Review the slide and propose an accessible six-week evaluation. This is a service-access exercise; do not use attendance as a measure of clinical need, merit, or consent.

facts.value: The service can sustain both phone and text for the next six weeks. It has no evidence that the 12 missing preferences mean a preferred channel.
facts.reveal_when: candidate asks about capacity or missing data

facts.value: The booking team can record chosen channel, attempted delivery, confirmed contact, and whether a person rescheduled. Individual reasons should be volunteered and summarized without unnecessary sensitive details.

model_points: The slide uses a true raw-count drop to imply an improvement that the denominators do not show. Neither the worse rate nor the lower count establishes the reminder effect.
The redesign must preserve a usable channel and collect missing preferences without assuming consent or access. Attendance is not an appropriate proxy for clinical priority or deservingness.
Recommend a limited evaluation using contact and rescheduling as well as attendance, with explicit capacity, interpretation limits, and a decision date.

probes.trigger: candidate fixes the percentage but immediately calls the redesign harmful
probes.question: What would the changed population and missing delivery data prevent you from concluding?

probes.trigger: candidate proposes a preference-first rollout rather than randomized allocation
probes.question: How would you describe the comparison limits while still learning from the rollout?

probes.trigger: candidate originally supports text-only then revises after considering unknown preferences
probes.question: Which slide recommendation and booking instruction must change?

fair_alternatives: A preference-first observational pilot or another ethical, accessible comparison may be accepted if causal limits and channel choice are explicit.
Candidates need not produce a statistical model; a useful decision plan with correct arithmetic is sufficient.

Assess the work demonstrated here. Accept relevant examples from education, volunteering, caregiving, placements, or paid work; professional vocabulary and employer pedigree are not evidence of a stronger answer.
reference.assessment_limits: Assess service access, data interpretation, and uncertainty. Do not infer clinical outcomes, legal messaging rules, or patient suitability from attendance. Unobserved dimensions are not failures. Credit a reasoned correction and distinguish independently demonstrated reasoning from coached assistance. Do not penalize a candidate for an unrevealed conditional fact; credit appropriate requests and conditional plans, and distinguish candidate assumptions from interviewer-supplied evidence.

interviewer_notes: Assess service access, data interpretation, and uncertainty. Do not infer clinical outcomes, legal messaging rules, or patient suitability from attendance. Use only the supplied fictional facts and policies; acknowledge unknowns. Ask one triggered probe at a time after the candidate has finished. Accept plain language and accessible written or spoken explanations. Do not score accent, typing speed, confidence, credentials, or experience with a named employer. Credit revisions and record assistance. All participants are fictional adults; no real patient, client, operational, or confidential data is needed. Allow silence for thinking without treating it as failure. In short sessions prioritize the core decision and one material follow-up, leaving room for a correction and wrap-up.

learning_drills.title: Rewrite the access slide
learning_drills.prompt: Replace the original slide with three observations, two unknowns, and one six-week decision checkpoint. This is self-guided practice; no model assessment is performed.
checklist: Separate missing preference from text choice
Measure contact rather than assume delivery
